description: We are a team of six with different skills, interests, and ideas, but one thing in common: we love creating things. We are especially interested in game development, technology, and engineering. Each of us has our own role and area of responsibility, which helps us bring different perspectives together. We enjoy experimenting, learning new things, and taking on challenges. We may come from different backgrounds, but we share the same curiosity and passion for turning ideas into reality.
summary: Space Mission: Alien is a multiplayer educational game combining social deduction with real-world space mission engineering. Players complete challenges inspired by NASA missions, including ISS energy management, life-support systems, Mars launch windows, and Voyager 1 spacecraft assembly. They explore engineering constraints, resource limitations, and technical decisions while working together to keep the mission running and identify hidden Aliens. The game features two worlds with 29 tasks each, online multiplayer, and AI practice mode.
details:
Space Mission: Alien - is a browser-based multiplayer social-deduction game where 4–8 players complete tasks inspired by real space engineering while one or two hidden Aliens sabotage the mission. Players explore pixel-art rooms, solve problems involving ISS battery power, Mars launch windows, signal delays, parity bits, and Voyager’s thrusters, then discuss suspicious behaviour and vote to eject suspects.

The game features two worlds and 58 tasks. On the Orbital Station, the crew wins by completing all tasks or ejecting every Alien. On SELENE Moon Base, players must complete all tasks and install 10 spacecraft parts to launch Voyager 1 in a fictional lunar scenario. Aliens win through numerical parity, two innocent-player ejections, an expired match timer, or unrepaired critical sabotage.

We assembled an extensive research database of mission facts, technical references, and source links, drawing on NASA, JPL, NTRS, ESA, JAXA, CSA, and materials covering space programmes in 12 additional countries. Every task’s factual basis is documented in SOURCES.md.

Our creative idea is that the task itself becomes a clue: understanding an engineering problem helps players complete the mission and question a teammate’s story. We aim to make mission engineering approachable for students and curious players while highlighting the global nature of space exploration.

We built the game using Node.js, the ws WebSocket library, JavaScript, HTML, CSS, WebAudio, and Python asset-preparation scripts. Shared rules keep online and bot modes consistent, server-side information filtering protects hidden roles, and automated WebSocket tests check multiplayer behaviour.

Our team considered factual accuracy, source traceability, fair play, configurable rules, bilingual access, and smaller screens. The current 0.5.0 beta supports English and Russian, public and private rooms, and a tutorial and bot practice that work without the online server. No account or installation is required.
